title: IT Inventory Manager
description: A command-line application for keeping device names, types, IP addresses, and locations in one database.
built: Designed a devices table with id, name, device_type, ip_address, and location fields.
Built a menu around adding, viewing, updating, and deleting devices. The shared code includes the menu and add-device implementation; final coverage of every action still needs confirmation.
Connected the Windows Python client to MySQL in a local Ubuntu VM. Used a forwarded localhost port while troubleshooting VM networking.
issues: Connection refused
Checked whether MySQL was reachable before debugging the application. A Windows Test-NetConnection check to localhost on TCP 3306 succeeded.
Parameterized SQL
Used %s placeholders and a separate values tuple with mysql.connector, keeping query structure separate from input.
lessons: Database persistence separates stored records from the Python program.
A successful port check verifies connectivity, while a query verifies the application/database path.

title: Proxmox Home Lab
description: A home server environment for experimenting with virtual machines, containers, and self-hosted services.
built: Used a Dell PowerEdge R630 with dual Xeon E5-2680 v4 processors as a lab platform.
Created Linux VMs and LXC containers for services including networking, game hosting, and application experiments.
Worked with Proxmox 8.4, storage allocation, CPU/RAM assignment, and network reachability. Hardware allocations have changed over time.
issues: Choosing VM or LXC
Compared the lighter resource footprint of containers with the isolation and full operating system of a VM.
Storage allocation
Investigated the difference between a virtual disk’s capacity and the space available inside a guest filesystem.
lessons: Virtualization lets one server support several independent experiments.
Document the guest, host, network, and storage layers separately when troubleshooting.

title: Cloud-to-Home Reverse Proxy
description: A cloud entry point connected to home-hosted applications through a Newt tunnel.
built: Hosted Pangolin on AWS EC2 and connected the home network through Newt.
Worked on routing to Proxmox, AMP, and a Next.js application.
Investigated the ongoing cost of the cloud endpoint after AWS credits, including local alternatives. Current hosting status needs an update.
issues: Proxmox upstream TLS
The Proxmox backend uses HTTPS on port 8006. Turning off upstream TLS led to a gateway timeout during troubleshooting.
Proxy routing
Worked through Traefik routers, upstream protocols, and certificate handling across several network hops.
lessons: A tunnel and a reverse proxy handle different parts of the request path.
Trace DNS, the public endpoint, tunnel connectivity, and backend reachability one hop at a time.

title: Local Reverse Proxy
description: Name-based access to applications inside the home network.
built: Moved toward LAN-only application access with Nginx Proxy Manager.
Configured DNS records to direct hostnames to a private reverse-proxy address.
Investigated name-resolution and browser connection errors while bringing the local route online.
issues: Wrong DNS target
A hostname resolved to 0.0.0.0. The A record was corrected to the intended LAN proxy address.
QUIC / connection errors
Checked name resolution and the intended local route while troubleshooting browser errors. The final browser configuration was not recorded.
lessons: A reverse-proxy rule cannot help if DNS sends the client to the wrong address.
Check hostname resolution before changing application settings.

title: WireGuard Remote Access
description: A self-hosted VPN for reaching home services from a phone and remote networks.
built: Ran WireGuard in the home lab, including Linux container-based setups.
Configured an iPhone peer and worked with endpoint, port, and routing settings.
Later explored access with the UDM Pro network. Exact current peer and routing configuration is not included here.
issues: Endpoint reachability
Worked with UDP 51820 and endpoint addressing. A private LAN endpoint only works directly from networks that can reach it.
Testing from outside
Cellular testing helps distinguish actual remote connectivity from a test made on the same home Wi-Fi.
lessons: VPN connectivity depends on both the tunnel handshake and routes to the destination.
Keep peer private keys and exported VPN configurations out of documentation.

title: Pi-hole & Recursive DNS
description: Network-wide DNS filtering paired with a local recursive resolver.
built: Ran Pi-hole on a Raspberry Pi and configured Unbound as a local resolver at 127.0.0.1:5335.
Used query logs and direct DNS tests to investigate failing domains and upstream behavior.
Worked through IPv6 DNS bypass, DNSSEC settings, and differences between container and Raspberry Pi deployments.
issues: SERVFAIL responses
Several domains failed while others resolved. Resolver settings and service restarts were part of the troubleshooting; the final complete configuration was not captured.
Clients bypassing Pi-hole
Investigated IPv6 DNS supplied by the router as a path around the configured Pi-hole resolver.
Filtering limits
DNS filtering cannot independently remove every advertisement served from the same domains as desired content.
lessons: Test the client, Pi-hole, and upstream resolver independently.
A successful lookup does not prove every device uses the intended DNS server.

title: Cisco Switching Lab
description: Hands-on managed-switch configuration with a Cisco WS-C2960X-48LPS-L.
built: Connected to the switch through a USB serial console, including a Windows COM7 session.
Worked with VLAN 1, management addressing, access/trunk concepts, and links to another switch.
Configured the switch hostname riverswitch and explored SSH management.
issues: Management access
Separated console access from IP-based management while learning initial switch configuration.
Uplink behavior
Investigated how access and trunk settings affect connectivity between switches. Final port assignments need to be recorded.
lessons: A switch’s management IP and its Layer 2 forwarding serve different purposes.
Record port roles and VLAN membership alongside configuration changes.

title: Dedicated Game Servers
description: A self-hosted environment for running and managing multiplayer game servers.
built: Used AMP while working with dedicated servers in the home lab.
Experimented with Minecraft variants including Spigot, Fabric, Pixelmon, and Cobblemon.
Worked on Satisfactory hosting, required ports, and connectivity. Separate instance versions and final configurations are still to be documented.
issues: Reachability
Investigated the relationship between application listeners, firewall rules, NAT, and client connections.
Modded environments
Worked with different Minecraft server ecosystems; each instance needs matching game, loader, and mod versions.
lessons: Test a game server on the LAN before diagnosing access from outside.
Keep a per-instance record of versions, ports, and world data.

title: Umbrel Bitcoin Node
description: A Bitcoin node experiment hosted in an UmbrelOS virtual machine.
built: Installed UmbrelOS in a virtual machine and worked with the Bitcoin node application.
Explored CPU and memory allocation, database cache, and a virtual disk around 1.3 TB.
Investigated Lightning and how its node operations differ from simply running Bitcoin Core.
issues: Guest disk capacity
Worked through a case where increasing virtual disk capacity did not immediately make all space usable inside the guest. Storage resizing was later reported resolved.
Ephemeral terminal changes
Umbrel warns that terminal modifications may not survive updates; persistent configuration requires care.
lessons: Node synchronization depends on storage and I/O as well as CPU and memory.
Separate VM disk size, partition size, and filesystem size when checking capacity.

title: Bitaxe Mining Experiment
description: A small mining hardware experiment focused on setup and performance troubleshooting.
built: Set up a Bitaxe 601 and investigated pool connectivity and reported hash rate.
Observed performance around 0.4 TH/s during troubleshooting.
Reported that restarting the device resolved the immediate performance issue.
issues: Low reported hash rate
A restart improved the reported issue. A sustained benchmark and final tuning values have not been recorded.
lessons: Short-term readings and long-term averages can tell different stories.
Record temperature, operating settings, and observation period when comparing performance.

title: Omarchy Virtual Machine
description: A Linux desktop experiment inside VirtualBox on a Windows laptop.
built: Installed Omarchy in a VirtualBox VM on the Lenovo laptop.
Worked through a blank desktop with a visible mouse cursor.
Reported a working Hyprland desktop after enabling software OpenGL; display scaling was the next adjustment.
issues: Blank graphical desktop
Kept VMSVGA, 128 MB display memory, and 3D acceleration, then added LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 through the Hyprland environment configuration.
Missing editor
The expected nano command was unavailable, requiring another way to edit the configuration.
lessons: A running cursor does not guarantee the desktop renderer initialized successfully.
Software rendering can help isolate a virtual GPU compatibility issue.

title: Container & Service Management
description: Experiments with packaging, managing, and routing self-hosted applications.
built: Worked with Docker Compose for Pangolin and its supporting services.
Used Portainer and explored Traefik routing for services such as AMP and Proxmox.
Investigated container networking, router configuration, and certificates. A complete inventory of Compose stacks has not yet been captured.
issues: Windows prerequisites
Docker reported missing virtualization support even though BIOS virtualization was enabled. Windows showed an active hypervisor, while WSL was not yet installed.
Service routes
Worked on matching hostnames and paths to the correct backend and protocol.
lessons: Host virtualization support and a working Docker backend are separate prerequisites.
Document volumes, networks, and environment variable names without exposing secret values.

title: Audio & Video Storage Calculator
description: A coursework script that calculates uncompressed media storage from recording settings.
built: Ran audio_storage.py in the NJIT AFS environment for IT101 homework.
Produced a table of sample rate, channel type, bit depth, duration, kilobytes, and megabytes.
Worked with variables, calculations, formatting, and a text file containing script execution instructions.
issues: Unit conversions
Connected bits per sample, samples per second, channels, and recording duration to storage size.
Remote execution
Used python3 with the script path on AFS and captured the output for the assignment.
lessons: State whether KB/MB use decimal or binary units.
Keep inputs and displayed precision clear so calculations can be checked.
